newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Most Eurobourses end higher, dollar weak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Most Eurobourses end higher, dollar weak.

text.p: Most of Europe's bourses closed higher on Friday, following two days of record closes on Wall Street, but early losses in the Dow Jones Industrial Average pulled European stocks off their session highs.

U.S. stocks led a worldwide rally in many equity markets this week, racking up hefty gains on the euphoria that followed the U.S. election, a positive earnings outlook from heavyweight Intel Corp and lower long-term rates in the U.S. bond market.
But one senior trader in London cautioned: "Wall Street has gained around 130 points in two days and it may take a bit of a breather...if it corrects heavily, we may come off a little."
By 1650 GMT, the Dow was down 14.91 points at 6,191.13, taking a rest from its four-day winning streak.
Further pressure on stocks could also emerge if the dollar fails to fully recover from Thursday's two-yen drop.
The dollar rose early in the day on reassuring comments from Japanese officials, including suggestions that Japan's interest rates would stay low for now.
But traders remained skeptical, and the dollar had drifted toward session lows again by late European trading.
"I think the dollar is likely to fall as far as 110.00 yen next week as a downward correction of the recent rally close to 115 yen," said a currency manager at a Japanese bank in Tokyo.
Stocks fared better with Germany's DAX index of 30 leading shares closing bourse trade at a record high of 2,739.83.
Dresdner Bank, Germany's third largest commercial bank, was among the biggest gainers in the DAX.

Dresdner shares ended up 1.39 at 42.89, the year's highest closing level, on news of plans to merge its global funds business. U.S. investment bank Salomon Bros also reiterated its buy recommendation on Dresdner.

In late Paris trading, the blue-chip CAC-40 slipped into negative territory after a positive start as investors sold some shares to lock in profits made during the index's near eight-percent run to around two-year highs this week. Investors were also squaring books before a three-day holiday weekend.
On Monday, France and Belgium celebrate Armistice Day and the U.S. celebrates Veteran's Day.

Dutch shares were boosted by strong third-quarter earnings from Unilever -- helped by some fund managers who, surprised by the market's strength, were forced to quickly buy shares so as not to miss the entire move up.
"Some people are having to pay up for stock they could have got a guilder cheaper yesterday," a Dutch dealer said.
British stocks ended modestly higher, but the outlook was clouded by inflation and interest rate fears.

The Confederation of British Industry said in a report that British retail sales for October rose at the fastest rate since 1988, which highlighted again the Bank of England's forecast on Wednesday that inflation and interest rates were set to rise.
"With inflation fears around, people are still scared this market will crack," said a senior equities dealer.
London traders were expected to stay sidelined before the policy-setting meeting U.S. Federal Open Market Committee on November 13, followed by the British budget on November 26.

"Consensus is still for no change (in U.S. rates), but the worry is that we are at the bottom of the rate cycle in the U.S. It's just a question of when a rate rise comes through," said SG Strauss Turnbull strategist Andy Hartwill.
Further worries that could cap gains on London's blue-chips came from sterling's recent surge, prompting fears the strong currency would start to carve into corporate earnings.
By 1645 GMT, sterling was at $1.6477, just softer than $1.6481 in late European trading on Thursday.
CURRENCIES AT 1645 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5047 marks and 111.54 yen, compared with 1.5073 marks and 111.38 yen in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE CLOSE
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares rose 10.4 points to 3,910.80.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index fell 6.61 points to 2,205.20
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index rose 26.61 to 2,739.83.
PRECIOUS METALS AT THE LONDON CLOSE
Gold closed at $379 nearly unchanged from Thursday's close of $379.45. Silver gained a cent to $4.81.
